meta.description: Identifies essential genes from CRISPR-Cas9 fitness screens using BAGEL2, a Bayesian classifier scoring per-gene Bayes Factors via log-likelihood ratios over per-sgRNA fold changes, calibrated against CEGv2 core-essentials and NEGv1 non-essentials. Covers fc+bf+pr workflow, tumor-suppressor detection, and BF calibration.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/p-values/effect sizes in any of the 5 outputs; all numbers traced to real BAGEL2/MAGeCK tool output on real HAP1 TKOv3 data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Basic-research gene-essentiality analysis; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 2's interpret_bagel() flags 86.5% of the genome as tumor-suppressor on a dropout screen, which is methodologically wrong taken alone, but the Skill's own Failure Modes section documents the exact caveat needed to avoid it (restrict TS calling to enrichment-designed screens). Scored as a P0 design gap rather than a veto-firing fabrication since the corrective information exists within the Skill.

code_usability.detail: All canonical-path code (BAGEL.py fc/bf/pr, interpret_bagel(), mageck test) ran with real installed tools; no syntax errors, no missing dependencies.

functional_suitability.note: fc/bf/pr, tumor-suppressor detection, calibration and MAGeCK/drugZ comparison all covered; but the reference-set failure-mode symptom described (Correctness) does not match observed behavior (crash / total-NaN corruption vs. the documented 'median near zero').

reliability.note: A species-mismatched reference set produces an uncaught scipy ValueError; swapped -e/-n arguments produce a silent, complete BF=nan corruption with exit 0 and no warning. Neither failure mode is caught or clearly reported by the Skill's guidance.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md concise (~250 lines), usage-guide and example script separated; linear fc->bf->pr workflow with no redundant steps.

agent_usability.note: Consistent terminology and clear output-format specs, but the per-sgRNA CLI flag (-r) needed for the Skill's own 'guide-of-one' diagnosis is never named, and Error Prevention misses the two concrete failure modes found in testing (reference-set crash, -e/-n swap, non-determinism, -NB 1000 runtime cost).

human_usability.note: Natural, precise trigger language. Strict input rejection is appropriate for scientific code (no penalty per Category 3 override), but when things do go wrong the failure is either a raw traceback or completely silent -- neither clearly identifies what's wrong to a human or agent.

security.note: No secrets, only public reference-data URLs. No pre-flight validation of column names or essential/non-essential reference-gene overlap before running, which is exactly what let the -e/-n swap corrupt silently.

maintainability.note: Clean separation of SKILL.md/usage-guide/example script and clear CLI parameterization, but outputs are not deterministic (Testability), undermining verifiability of any single run.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger, good progressive disclosure, clean composability with hit-calling/pathway-analysis Skills; but the skill is not idempotent (confirmed non-determinism) and its escape-hatch/failure-mode guidance is incomplete for the two concrete corruption/crash paths found in testing.

inputs.label: Per-sgRNA BF (-r) diagnosis + determinism check
inputs.note: The undocumented -r flag was required to get per-sgRNA contributions; identical bf reruns with no seed differed by up to 26.7 BF and flipped 33 genes across the BF>6 threshold.

assertions.text: SKILL.md documents the CLI flag needed for per-sgRNA Bayes Factor contributions
assertions.note: Not documented anywhere; found only via BAGEL.py bf --help (-r/--sgrna-bayes-factors).

assertions.text: Per-sgRNA BF contributions sum approximately to the gene-level BF
assertions.note: RPS3: sum of 4 per-sgRNA BFs = 78.9 vs gene-level 80.8, confirming the additive-LLR model.

assertions.text: Skill documents that default runs are non-deterministic and recommends a fixed seed for reproducible calls
assertions.note: Not mentioned anywhere; default seed is time.time()-based.

assertions.text: Repeat-run BF differences are consistent with the CV-split design, not a code bug
assertions.note: Differences are of the magnitude expected from 10-fold CV resampling variance, not a logic error.

key_strengths: Full fc->bf->pr pipeline runs end-to-end on real 70,754-sgRNA HAP1 TKOv3 data; top Bayes-Factor genes (POLR2L, POLR3H, GTPBP10, mitochondrial ribosomal proteins) match independently-recorded ground truth and cross-validate against a separately-run MAGeCK analysis.
Tumor-suppressor detection claim is genuinely validated: TSC1/TSC2 are among the most negative-BF genes and independently confirmed by MAGeCK's positive-selection call on the same data.
BAGEL2-vs-MAGeCK reconciliation claim is empirically correct: BAGEL2 recovers 99.5% of MAGeCK's significant hits while calling 2.1x as many total hits, exactly as the comparison table predicts.
PR-curve-based BF ladder (0/6/12/30) is empirically well-calibrated against real data, with precision approximately 1.0 at BF>=6.

recommendations.title: BAGEL2 results are non-deterministic and the Skill never says so
recommendations.problem: Identical `BAGEL.py bf` invocations on the same data differ by up to 26.7 BF and flip 33 genes across the BF>6 essential/non-essential threshold, because BAGEL.py's default seed is time.time()-based.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md, usage-guide.md and the shipped run_bagel2.sh example all omit the -s/--seed flag.
recommendations.fix: Add `-s <fixed-int>` to every bf example invocation and a Validation Checklist item requiring a recorded seed for any 'publication-quality' or clinical-grade call.

recommendations.title: interpret_bagel() produces scientifically absurd output on the Skill's own benchmarked dataset
recommendations.problem: Running the Skill's own interpret_bagel() code on a real dropout screen (BF<-6 threshold) flags 86.5% of the genome as tumor-suppressor, with three assay control constructs (LacZ, luciferase, EGFP) as the top hits.
recommendations.root_cause: The runnable code sample implements no screen-design guard or control-gene filter, even though the Failure Modes section elsewhere in the same document correctly documents both the risk and the fix.
recommendations.fix: Move the screen-design check and a control-gene exclusion list directly into interpret_bagel(), and add a sanity assertion that warns when more than a small percentage of genes are flagged as tumor suppressor.

recommendations.title: Reference-set failure modes are documented inaccurately
recommendations.problem: The Common Errors/Failure Modes table predicts 'median BF near zero, no hits' for a bad reference set, but actual behavior is either an uncaught crash (species mismatch) or silent total BF=nan corruption across every gene (swapped -e/-n arguments, never mentioned at all).
recommendations.root_cause: Guidance appears to be written from theory rather than tested against these concrete misconfigurations.
recommendations.fix: Add the -e/-n argument-swap case to Common Errors with its actual symptom (all-NaN output, exit 0), and correct or qualify the 'near zero' claim for a genuine reference mismatch.

recommendations.title: Per-sgRNA diagnostic flag is undocumented
recommendations.problem: The 'Bayesian Reasoning Per Sgrna' section and the 'guide-of-one' diagnosis both depend on per-sgRNA BF output, but the required -r/--sgrna-bayes-factors CLI flag is never named in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.
recommendations.root_cause: The section describes the underlying concept but omits the concrete invocation.
recommendations.fix: Add `BAGEL.py bf ... -r` explicitly to that section's example, alongside the RNA/GENE/BF output schema it produces.

recommendations.title: STD/NumObs output columns silently depend on an unstated flag
recommendations.problem: The usage-guide calls the STD column 'the diagnostic for guide-quality issues,' but that column only exists under -b (bootstrap) mode, not the CV mode described as the default; -NB 1000 also takes roughly 20-25 minutes at genome scale with no runtime-cost warning given.
recommendations.root_cause: Prose describing the 'default' resampling mode is inconsistent with the Output columns table, which implicitly assumes bootstrap output.
recommendations.fix: State explicitly that STD/NumObs require -b, and add a runtime-cost note for -NB 1000 on genome-scale libraries.
